task: predict RPE1 perturbation profile similarity; edges are K562-derived so this is out-of-sample
verdict: THE PARTNERS ARE USED; THE SIGN IS NOT. Swapping unsigned context for the perturbational layer's partners is worth +0.0521, but PERMUTING THE SIGNS of those same partners costs only +0.0049 -- the shuffled arm retains 91% of the gain. What the model uses is WHICH genes a knockout is linked to and how strongly, not which way it moves them. Partner identity is worth +0.1172 against random partners of the same count, which is where nearly all the signal lives. AND THE ARCHITECTURE IS A NET LOSS ON THIS TASK: the best transformer arm sits -0.0177 against a plain MLP on the perturbed gene's own features, and the self-only transformer is -0.0950 behind it.
verdict_correction: The first run's verdict read 'THE SIGN IS USED' from +0.0049 against a 0.0022 seed spread while the shuffled-sign control retained 94% of the effect. No measurement changed; only its reading was wrong, and the module's threshold now requires three seed spreads AND a quarter of the signed-over-unsigned gain before the sign can be called used.
